newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium futures rise in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium futures rise in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures rose in lacklustre trade on Thursday, with support provided by the solid performance overnight on the LME and the dollar's rally, traders said.
"I feel they're (aluminium futures) overbought," said one trader. "As volume's very thin, prices tend to move in strides," he said.

Traders said the dollar's recovery following a slump on Tuesday helped market participants look at positive market factors, such as the LME's recent healthy performance and the U.S. decision earlier this week to leave interest rates unchanged.
By late Tokyo on Thursday, the dollar rallied more than one yen towards 116 yen.
Benchmark April 1998 gained by 3.8 yen to 195.2 yen per kg, recovering most of its losses made since the dollar started its downward trend last Friday.
April hit its contract low of 190.4 yen on Tuesday. Other contracts ranged from 1.4 to 4.3 yen higher.
Estimated trade volume shrank to 2,643 lots from 3,331 lots on Wednesday.
